operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
1. There is hereby created, for the du­
ration of the war and six months there­
after, a National Railway Labor Panel  
of nine members, hereinafter referred to
as the Panel, to be appointed by the Pres­
ident, and to be qualified as to member­
ship thereon in the same manner as pro­
vided in Section 10 of the Railway Labor  
Act for membership on emergency boards. 
The President shall designate a chairman 
from the members of the Panel and shall  
fill vacancies thereon as they may occur.  
The Chairman of the Panel shall receive  
such compensation, together with neces­
sary travelling expenses, as the President  
may prescribe. The members of the  
Panel shall receive necessary travel ex­
penses and subsistence expenses or per  
diem allowances in lieu thereof on such  
days as they are actually engaged in per­
formance of duties pursuant to this Or­
der.

2. Whenever a dispute between a car­
rier or carriers and its or their employees  
concerning changes in rates of pay, rules,  
or working conditions, or whenever any  
other dispute not referable to the Na­
tional Railroad Adjustment Board, is not  
adjusted or settled under the provisions  
of Sections 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 of the Railway  
Labor Act, the duly designated and au­
thorized representatives of employees in­
volved in such dispute may, prior to no­
tice by the National Mediation Board to  
the President, of a threatened interrup­
tion to commerce, notify the Chairman  
of the Panel of the failure of the parties  
to adjust the dispute and of their desire  
to avoid the taking of a strike vote and  
the setting of a strike date. If, in the  
judgment of the Chairman of the Panel,  
the dispute is such that if unadjusted,  
even in the absence of a strike vote, it  
may interfere with the prosecution of  
the war, he may thereupon select three  
members of the Panel to serve as an  
emergency board to investigate such dis­
pute and to report thereon to the Presi­
dent. Subject to the provisions of Sec­
tion 10, such board shall have exclusive  
and final jurisdiction of the dispute and  
shall make every reasonable effort to  
settle such dispute.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9883 is a bare revocation with no savings, transition or winding-up clause. EO 9172 itself contains none: it created the National Railway Labor Panel and its emergency boards, which existed only to investigate and report on disputes; reports already made were completed acts, and nothing in either order preserves pending board proceedings, pay or any right. Rail disputes reverted to the Railway Labor Act procedures that EO 9883's recital names as adequate.

research_rationale: EO 9172 (May 22, 1942) created a National Railway Labor Panel 'for the duration of the war and six months thereafter' and let its chairman form three-member emergency boards (paras. 1-3; 7 FR 3913-3914, read in the held govinfo scan). Before taking the revocation as the first end I checked the order's own term: the state of war with Germany and Japan had not been terminated in August 1947 (the President's proclamation of December 31, 1946 ended only hostilities), so the Panel's own term had not run, and EO 9883's recital confirms the Panel still existed. No amendment or partial revocation is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification disposition table, a lead only). EO 9883 (12 FR 5481) revokes the order outright, states no effective date and has no savings clause, so every paragraph ended on its signing date, August 11, 1947. The U.S. Code and eCFR machine searches found no current citation.

research_rationale: EO 9635 (September 29, 1945) reorganized the Navy Department in ten numbered paragraphs, read in the held govinfo scan of 10 FR 12419 and its continuation on 12421. It has no expiry or condition of its own. Its main statutory basis, Title I of the First War Powers Act, was by its sec. 401 in force during the war and for six months after its termination; the war had not been terminated by April 1950, and EO 10123 treats the order as still in force, so no earlier statutory lapse is shown. The one earlier event is EO 9904 (November 13, 1947), which replaced the text of para. 8 (order of succession), so the original para. 8 ended on that date. EO 10123 (15 FR 2265) then revoked EO 9635 and EO 9904 without a stated effective date, so every other paragraph ended on its signing date, April 20, 1950, which is the whole-order end. The National Security Act of 1947 and its 1949 amendments, which reorganized the military establishment, were not read here; no held source (OFR catalog, U.S. Code notes, 1989 Codification table) records that they revoked or replaced any paragraph, which is a limit of this bounded search rather than a finding. Savings: EO 10123 keeps EOs 8984 and 9096 revoked (non-revival), an effect now resting on EO 10123. The OFR catalog and the 1989 Codification table (a lead) list no other amendment.

§  6 .1  Authority to except positions  
from the competitive service,  (a) The 
Commission is authorized to except from 
the competitive service and to place in 
appropriate schedules positions to which 
appointments through competitive ex­
amination are not practicable and, upon 
the recommendation of the agency con­
cerned, positions which are of a confi­
dential or policy-determining character. 
Such exceptions from the competitive 
service shall be effective upon publica­
tion thereof in the F ederal  R egister . 
Positions excepted by the Commissi on 
shall be listed in the Commission’s an­
nual report for the fiscal year in which 
the exceptions are made.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10577 sec. 301 attaches a proviso to its revocations: positions listed in Schedules A, B and C 'as provided for in Civil Service Rule VI of that order, as amended' (that is, Rule VI as rewritten by EO 10440, which created Schedule C) 'shall be considered as being listed in Schedules A, B, and C, respectively,' of the new Rule VI, unless and until the Commission removes them. The Commission's schedule placements made under EO 10440 were therefore carried into EO 10577's schedules; they continue, if at all, under EO 10577 and later rules, not under EO 10440. No other savings clause was found.

unresolved_material_gaps: EO:10440#sec2: date on which the Commission completed the reclassification directed by sec. 2 (when the transitional rule was spent) not established from held sources; it ended no later than January 23, 1955 (EO 10577).
research_rationale: EO 10440 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823-1824, read in the held govinfo scan) rewrote Civil Service Rule VI (secs. 6.1-6.6, creating Schedule C) and in sec. 2 directed the Commission to reclassify existing Schedule A and B positions, keeping them in place until it acted. Earlier events: EO 10463 (June 25, 1953) replaced sec. 6.4, so the original sec. 6.4 ended that day. The other Rule VI sections continued until EO 10577 sec. 301 revoked EO 10440 by name, effective (sec. 401) on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after November 22, 1954, i.e. January 23, 1955, which is therefore the whole-order end (no later-ending clause exists). Sec. 2 is a transitional direction that was spent once the Commission had reclassified every listed position; the date that happened is not in the held sources, so its first end is left open rather than set to the revocation date. Savings: EO 10577's proviso carried the schedule listings into the new rules.

research_rationale: EO 10898 (December 2, 1960; 25 FR 12429, read in the held govinfo scan) established the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board of cabinet officers (sec. 1), gave it coordinating and study functions (sec. 2), provided agency assistance (sec. 3), made it advisory only (sec. 4) and required reports (sec. 5). It has no term of its own. Earlier clause-level ends: EO 10986 (January 12, 1962) substituted a new sec. 1(b), so the original membership list ended then; EO 11382 sec. 8 (November 28, 1967) struck all of sec. 1(b) as amended and changed the quorum in sec. 1(d) from three to four, so the original quorum rule ended then. EO 11382 sec. 16(3) also revoked EO 10858, which sec. 4 cites for the President's Committee for Traffic Safety; this is recorded as a later event on sec. 4, but the section's main rule (Board advisory only) continued. EO 11515 (March 13, 1970) terminated the Board and revoked EO 10898 and EO 10986 without a stated effective date, so the remaining clauses ended on March 13, 1970, the whole-order end. The Board consisted of federal officials and ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies.

research_rationale: EO 11126 (November 1, 1963; 28 FR 11717-11718, read in the held govinfo scan) set up an Interdepartmental Committee on the Status of Women of cabinet officers (Part I) and a Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women (Part II), with support provisions (Part III). It has no term of its own. Clause-level history: EO 11221 (May 6, 1965) substituted new texts for secs. 101(a), 103 and 201, so the original texts ended then. The Council was an advisory committee in existence on January 5, 1973 and would have expired under sec. 14(a)(1) of the Federal Advisory Committee Act on January 5, 1975, but EO 11827 (signed January 4, 1975) continued it to January 5, 1977 and EO 11948 (effective December 31, 1976) to December 31, 1978, so there was no statutory lapse. EO 12007 (August 22, 1977) terminated the Council and revoked sec. 102(5) and Part II and rewrote sec. 103 and the second sentence of sec. 301, so those clauses ended then. The Committee clauses (federal officials, outside the Act) continued until EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11126 as amended, signed April 4, 1978 with no other effective date stated: that is the whole-order end. None of these orders contains a savings clause.

unresolved_material_gaps: Public Law 94-167 (89 Stat. 1003), the statute under which the Commission operated after 1975, is not held and was not read; its duration and termination terms decide when the Commission clauses (secs. 1(a), 1(c), 1(d), 2(a)-(g), 3) ended (on or before April 4, 1978).

research_rationale: EO 11832 (January 9, 1975; 40 FR 2415-2417, read in the held govinfo scan) established the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975 (secs. 1-3) and an interdepartmental task force (sec. 4). Exact clause-level ends found: EO 11889 (November 25, 1975) replaced the original sec. 2(h), which had ended the Commission's work with 1975; EO 11979 (March 28, 1977) replaced the original sec. 1(b) membership rule (further amended by EO 11980). The other clauses are certainly terminated by the cutoff, since EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11832 as amended on April 4, 1978, but that revocation may be a clean-up. Under EO 11889 the Commission was to end after a final report due within thirty days after June 30, 1976. EO 11979 shows it was still operating in 1977 'in accord with Section 2' of Public Law 94-167, which directed it to organize the National Women's Conference, and the Commission was set up after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect, so sec. 14(a)(2) of that Act also bears on its duration. Without reading Public Law 94-167, which states how long the Commission lasted and when it ended, the first ends of the Commission and task-force clauses, the whole-order end and the savings question cannot be fixed honestly; they are left open.

research_rationale: EO 11534 (June 4, 1970; 35 FR 8865, read in the held govinfo scan) created a National Council on Organized Crime of eighteen named federal officials to formulate a national strategy against organized crime. It has no term, report deadline or condition, and no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead). EO 12110 sec. 1-103(c) lists it among orders 'that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed'. That recital gives no date and is not itself a legal act ending the Council earlier; the order's own terms set no end, and the Council, composed wholly of full-time federal officers, was outside the termination rule of sec. 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (the continuance orders EO 11827 and EO 11948 accordingly do not list it). The legal first end of every clause is therefore the revocation, effective December 31, 1978 under sec. 1-105. Changes in some members' offices (for example the Post Office Department and the Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs were later reorganized) altered who sat on the Council but did not end it; they were not separately researched.

First end of every clause not established. EO 12110 sec. 1-103 (effective 1978-12-31) revoked the order as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', so the revocation is probably a clean-up. If the Commission was an advisory committee subject to the Federal Advisory Committee Act, it terminated under sec. 14(a)(1) (held 86 Stat. 776) and EO 11827 sec. 4 on January 5, 1975, since EO 11827 did not continue it. Whether the Act applied to this mixed dispute-settlement and advisory body has not been established.

research_rationale: EO 11482 (September 22, 1969; 34 FR 14723-14725, read in the held govinfo scan) created a tripartite Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission with study, recommendation, dispute-intercession, rule-making and reporting functions (secs. 1-9). Clause inventory from the official scan, with each provision quoted from one page. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(a) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 (sec. 1-105) as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', so the revocation is likely a clean-up after an earlier end. The candidate earlier end is statutory: under Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(1), advisory committees in existence on January 5, 1973 terminated on January 5, 1975 unless renewed, and EO 11827 sec. 4 says the same of presidential committees it did not continue; EO 11827 did not continue this Commission. Whether the Act reached this body, which mediated and intervened in disputes as well as advising, is a legal question left open, so first ends are not asserted. The CONFLICT (29 CFR part 901 still cites the order) is left open because the eCFR text is not on this machine.

unresolved_material_gaps: First end of every clause not established. The Committee (ten labor and ten management members appointed by the President) was created April 1, 1975, after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect; under its sec. 14(a)(2) (held 86 Stat. 776) such a committee terminates not later than two years after establishment unless renewed. EO 11948 (effective 1976-12-31), the general continuance order, did not renew it, and EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) describes it as terminated or its work completed. Whether the Act applied and whether any separate renewal was made has not been established, so the expiry date (about April 1, 1977) is not asserted.
whole_order_end not set until the first-end question is resolved (latest possible date 1978-12-31, EO 12110).
research_rationale: EO 11849 (April 1, 1975; 40 FR 14887-14888, read in the held govinfo scan) created the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction (secs. 1-6). The order has no term of its own. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', which signals an earlier end. The likely earlier end is the two-year limit of Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(2), since the general continuance order of December 1976 (EO 11948) did not renew it. Because the Act's application and the absence of any other renewal are not proven from held sources, first ends and the whole-order end are left open. Savings: none found. The U.S. Code note (29 U.S.C. 171 note) and the eCFR hits are historical and report the revocation; no CONFLICT is open.

unresolved_material_gaps: Actual date of submission of the Committee's report (due no later than June 11, 1977 under EO 11982) and any presidential extension under sec. 3(b) not established; the Committee terminated thirty days after submission unless extended, so the first end of the clauses tied to its existence cannot be dated. research_rationale: EO 11971 (February 11, 1977; 42 FR 9155-9156, read in the held govinfo scan) created a temporary Committee on Selection of the Director of the FBI (secs. 1-7). Sec. 3(b) makes it terminate thirty days after it submits its report unless the President extends it. EO 11982 (April 29, 1977) replaced the original sec. 3(a), so that clause's first end is exact. All other clauses depended on the Committee's existence, which ended under the order's own terms at a date not recorded in held sources, or, if extended, no later than EO 12110's revocation effective December 31, 1978. EO 12110 itself describes the Committee as terminated or its work completed. Those first ends and the whole-order end are left open rather than inferred from the June 11, 1977 deadline. Savings: none found.

A deadline does not prove the report date. EO 12110 (effective 1978-12-31) describes it as terminated or its work completed.

research_rationale: EO 11973 (February 17, 1977; 42 FR 10677-10678, read in the held govinfo scan) established the President's Commission on Mental Health (secs. 1-9). Sec. 9 makes it terminate sixty days after it transmits its final report, which sec. 3 required by April 1, 1978. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(e) later revoked the order, effective December 31, 1978, as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed'; the revocation is therefore a clean-up after the termination under sec. 9. Because the transmittal date is not in held sources and must not be inferred from the deadline, the first ends and the whole-order end are left open. The Commission was within the two-year limit of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, so no statutory termination intervened. Savings: none found.

military compensation issues, specifically addressing the following issues:
( 1  ) What form of military compensation is the most effective for meeting the 
needs of the Nation in peace and war? Is the present pay and allowances system ap­

potential to serve the national purpose?

cial and incentive pays) and what are the appropriate criteria for using them?

pensation system, and, if so, how?

research_rationale: EO 11998 (June 27, 1977; 42 FR 33021-33022, read in the held govinfo scan) established the President's Commission on Military Compensation (secs. 1-9). Sec. 9 makes it terminate thirty days after it submits its report, which sec. 2(c) required by March 15, 1978. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(f) revoked the order effective December 31, 1978 as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', a clean-up after the termination under sec. 9. The submission date is not in held sources and must not be inferred from the deadline, so first ends and the whole-order end are left open. The Commission was within the two-year limit of the Federal Advisory Committee Act. The U.S. Code note at 37 U.S.C. 1009 is historical and reports the revocation. Savings: none found.

research_rationale: EO 7972 (September 15, 1938; 3 FR 2249-2252, read in the held govinfo scan) prescribed regulations for paying currency-appreciation losses of officers, enlisted men and employees serving abroad (secs. 1-7), with a table of basic rates in sec. 4. It was amended by EOs 8018 (new sec. 3(h)), 8261 (additions to sec. 1(b); new sec. 2(b)), 8269 (complete new rate table, effective December 1, 1939), 8800, 9057 and 9261 (table entries) and 9449 (new sec. 2(b) and conflict amendment, effective July 1, 1944), and was revoked with all of them by EO 9687. Exact clause-level ends: the original sec. 2(b) ended September 21, 1939 (EO 8261) and the original rate table December 1, 1939 (EO 8269). The other clauses lasted until EO 9687, whose effective date is set agency by agency at the close of the pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946, so no single exact date can be asserted. EO 9449's conflict amendment also cut back several clauses for War and Navy personnel from July 1, 1944, to an extent not delimited here. Sec. 7's supersession of EO 6928 was a one-time disposition; EO 9687 does not say whether its revocation revives earlier orders, and none was found to have been revived. The first ends, whole-order end and savings are left open.

EO 9449 (effective July 1, 1944) made no losses payable to most War and Navy Department personnel and by its sec. 2 amended 'accordingly' every conflicting provision of EO 7972 as amended; how far that implied amendment ended the clauses marked with the EO 9449 later event has not been delimited.

savings_residuals not closed: EO 9687 has no savings clause; whether claims for currency-appreciation losses that accrued before each agency's effective date remained payable (accrued rights under the Act of March 26, 1934, as amended) has not been established.
research_rationale: EO 8261 (September 21, 1939; 4 FR 4043, read in the held govinfo scan) has two operative paragraphs: para. 1 adds ship definitions to sec. 1(b) of EO 7972, and para. 2 substitutes a new sec. 2(b). EO 9449 para. 1, 'effective as of July 1, 1944', again replaced sec. 2(b), so para. 2 ended exactly on July 1, 1944. Para. 1 remained in EO 7972, though EO 9449's conflict amendment cut back its use for Navy ship personnel to an extent not delimited here, until EO 9687 revoked EO 8261 by name, effective agency by agency at the close of the pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946. That date cannot be fixed as one exact date, so para. 1's first end, the whole-order end and savings are left open.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Title 5, Section 118c), Executive Order 
No. 7972 of September 15, 1938,1  as 
amended, prescribing regulations gov­
erning payment of losses sustained by 
officers, enlisted men, and employees of 
the United States in foreign countries on 
account of appreciation of foreign cur­
rencies in their relation to the American 
dollar, is hereby further amended, effec­
tive as of July 1,1944, as follows:
1. Section 2 (b) of the said Executive 
Order is amended to read as follows:
In case of officers, enlisted men, and 
employees serving under the War or Navy 
Departments (with the exception of per­
sonnel of military and naval missions, 
military and naval attaches, naval ob­
servers, port directors and other persons 
attached to their offices, and other of­
ficers, enlisted men, and employees when 
designated by the Secretary of War or 
the Secretary of the Navy, who shall be 
governed by paragraph (a) of this sec­
tion) , no losses shall be payable.

of the said Executive Order No. 7972, as 
amended, so far as they are in conflict 
with the provisions of this order, are
